bibliographic.title: Large language models for clinical artificial intelligence in healthcare: a systematic review
bibliographic.citation_apa: Ghnemat, R., & Saleh, A. (2026). Large language models for clinical artificial intelligence in healthcare: A systematic review. Discover Artificial Intelligence, 6, 156. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44163-025-00784-x

methodology.sample_description: 246 records identified between January 2020 and September 2025; 90 studies included after full-text screening
methodology.technology_context: Large Language Models (LLMs), Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), generative AI, transformer-based architectures, prompting, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), multi-agent (agentic) workflows, NLP

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed systematic review of LLMs and MLLMs in healthcare that explicitly addresses ethical governance frameworks, deployment, RAG, multi-agent workflows, hallucinations, bias, privacy, and regulatory compliance. It aligns with regulated-domain LLM governance themes but the available text does not establish conversational AI or conversational governance as a primary focus; it appears broader clinical LLM synthesis rather than central evidence on conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter/page 1 was provided; full-text sections on governance, deployment, RAG, and conversational or agentic workflows were not available for verification.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on page 1 (title, abstract, keywords). The review reports clear scope and inclusion counts, but search strategy, quality appraisal of included studies, and synthesis methods are not visible in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: The abstract presents a coherent systematic review with defined record counts and healthcare focus, but methodological detail and conversational-governance specificity are insufficient in the provided excerpt to support high confidence.

coding.theme: Systematic synthesis of LLMs and MLLMs for clinical artificial intelligence in healthcare
coding.subtheme: Governance, deployment, and risk considerations for generative AI in medicine

synthesis.main_claim: This systematic review synthesizes 90 included studies (from 246 records, January 2020–September 2025) on the clinical role of LLMs and MLLMs in healthcare, covering technical foundations, construction, evaluation, deployment, multimodal integration, RAG, multi-agent workflows, and governance-related risks and recommendations.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a consolidated, evidence-based overview of GenAI/LLM advances in medicine with emphasis on multimodal integration, ethical governance frameworks, prompting/RAG/multi-agent methods, and actionable guidance for clinicians, developers, and policymakers on safe integration and regulatory compliance.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text does not describe full review methods, quality assessment of included studies, or detailed findings/limitations sections; conversational governance is not explicitly framed as the primary object of study.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for healthcare-regulated LLM deployment, governance frameworks, RAG/agentic workflows, and compliance-oriented recommendations; not as central primary evidence for conversational governance unless later sections explicitly address chatbots, dialogue systems, or conversational oversight.
